extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent attorneys/agents and applicants (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for maintaining and documenting the electronic image file wrapper and search records during patent examination (MPEP §719). Primarily instructs examiners how to record classification, searches, claim indexing, residence changes, and when/what to include in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image file wrapper is the official record
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic file record in which the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office maintains the application papers is referred to as an image file wrapper. The electronic file record is the official record of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the image file wrapper as the official record of the application (see MPEP §202). Do not alter the official status of the electronic file record; all appropriate notations (e.g., benefit/priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119, 120, 121, 365, 386) should be made in the file history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers in image file wrapper — do not enter non-permanent papers / expungement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that do not become a permanent part of the record should not be entered as a paper in the image file wrapper. No paper legally entered in the image file wrapper should ever be withdrawn or expunged from the application file, especially a part of the original disclosure of the application, without special authority of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.59 provides limited exceptions (e.g., unintentionally submitted documents or proprietary information not important to patentability) where expungement may be allowed. See MPEP §724 for handling proprietary/trade secret materials and petitions to expunge. Avoid entering transient/non-permanent materials into the image file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers not returned — Form paragraph 7.214 and copies at applicant expense
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers in an application that has received a filing date ordinarily will not be returned. If applicant has not preserved copies of the papers, the Office will furnish copies at applicant’s expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.214 to notify applicants that papers ordinarily will not be returned. Refer applicants to 37 CFR 1.19 for copying fees and to MPEP §724.05 for petitions to expunge or obtain copies. This is particularly relevant for pro se filers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence of inventor changed — when to change records and publication/issuance timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless specifically requested by applicant, the residence(s) associated with the inventor(s) will not be changed. For a patent application publication to be published with residence information that differs from that originally filed, the revised information must be entered into the Office electronic records at least nine weeks before the publication date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012, to have a patent issue with a new residence applicants must file a corrected Application Data Sheet (37 CFR 1.76(c)) showing the new residence information with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for text removed (see MPEP §601.05(a)). For applications filed prior to that date, applicants are encouraged to file a Supplemental ADS (see MPEP §601.05(b)). Do not change residence fields unless expressly requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification recorded when application received
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new application is received in a Technology Center, the classification of the application and the initials or name of the examiner who will examine it or other assigned docket designation are noted in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper initial classification entry (see also MPEP §909.01(b)). Record who will examine the application (initials/name) or other docket designation so there is a clear record of assignment and classification at intake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index of Claims must be updated with each Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Index of Claims' found in the image file wrapper of an application should be updated with each Office action to maintain a reliable index of all claims in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the claim numbers as they appear during prosecution, track status of each claim in adjacent columns, and fill the final column with final patent claim numbers at allowance. Provide dates of each Office action and resulting status; place final patent claim numbers in the 'Final' column upon allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of Search — record areas searched, dates, and examiner initials
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on the merits of an application, the examiner must record in the appropriate sections of the Official Correspondence 'Search Notes' form the areas in which the search for prior art was made. The examiner must also indicate the date(s) on which the search was conducted and provide their initials. In subsequent actions where the search is updated, indicate that the search has been updated and identify additional fields of search with date and initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the appropriate databases, search queries, and classifications employed in the original search. Great care should be taken to clearly indicate the places searched and the date(s) on which the search was conducted or updated. A complete record of what was searched is important for evaluating patent strength/validity (especially in litigation). Searches are listed in the 'SEARCHED' boxes and/or 'SEARCH NOTES' box of the 'Search Notes' form. When limited electronic searches are performed, include a search history printout in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entries in 'SEARCHED' boxes — how to record classification searches and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Search Notes form includes 'SEARCHED' boxes for recording searches in CPC, CPC Combination Sets and USPC. When documenting a classification search, the examiner should ensure the proper box(es) is/are used. When a classification search is performed, the classification symbol must be recorded in the appropriate 'SEARCHED' box along with the date and the examiner’s initials. When a classification search is limited, the examiner must ensure that how the search was limited is made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the search was limited, include a search history printout with the 'Search Notes' form or annotate the 'SEARCH NOTES' box to indicate how it was limited. It is inaccurate to merely record the classification symbol without including the printout or limitation explanation unless all documents for that classification location were reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entries in 'SEARCH NOTES' box — required formats and types of entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries made in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box are intended to complete the application file record of areas and/or documents considered by the examiner in their search. The examiner will record specific types of information in the 'SEARCH NOTES' box, each entry dated and initialed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required entries include (A) annotations indicating how a classification search was limited; (B) notation 'See search history printout(s)' for text searches where no classification search was performed (and include the printout); (C) searches within the IPC; (D) searches performed by STIC (record 'See search history printout(s)' and date); (E) consultations with other examiners (record class/subclass and '(consulted)', may include name and art unit); (F) searches in electronic journals/books (include printouts/history); (G) searches in other media/databases (record unique identification, query, location/form e.g., CD-ROM); (H) Internet searches — print the first page and any subsequent pages with webpages reviewed, ensure search engine name, search logic and date are present or write them on the printout, indicate all webpages reviewed; (I) nonelectronic searches of print materials — record titles/terms/periods/volumes/pages as appropriate (examples provided); (J) review of art cited in parent/original patent files — record application/patent number followed by 'refs. checked' and note exceptions; (K) review of documents cited in related PTAB trials where claims DO NOT have similar scope — record trial number and U.S. Patent on trial and date reviewed; (L) review of documents cited in related PTAB trials where claims DO HAVE similar scope — record trial number, document reviewed, U.S. Patent on trial and date reviewed. Use examples/formats provided in MPEP for each type. All entries should be dated and initialed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search history printouts — minimum required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any time that a limited electronic search was performed (e.g., limited classified search or text search), a complete search history in the form of a printout must be included in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The search history must include at minimum: (A) all the search logic or chemical structure or sequence(s) used as a database query; (B) all the name(s) of the file(s) searched and the database service; (C) the date the search was made or updated; and (D) an indication of the examiner who performed the search (e.g., user ID or examiner’s initials). Do not merely list the tool/database name; supply the history/printout. Printouts should be devoid of result printouts to limit 'bulk search printouts.' For nucleotide/peptide sequence searches, include the full printout up to the 'ALIGNMENTS' section. If multiple search statements exist, indicate which statement(s) produced the results reviewed. Table 1 of the section lists history commands for common database services and the included elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference search history requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is in condition for allowance, an interference search must be made by using the most efficient and effective manner based on the claimed subject matter in the broadest claim (e.g., text search, classified search, or combination). Examiners are reminded that continuation-in-part applications may contain claims entitled to different effective filing dates and each effective filing date should be considered when performing the interference search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application contains a claim directed to a nucleotide or peptide sequence, request STIC to perform an interference search of the sequence. Record completion of the interference search in the 'INTERFERENCE SEARCH' section of the 'Search Notes' form and identify the manner in which it was limited (if any). Make of record a printout showing only the database(s) searched, the query(ies) used (if any), and the date the interference search was performed. Do not place result printouts of the interference search in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information not recorded in the application file (IDS consideration reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an indication of consideration or nonconsideration of prior art citations submitted by applicant in Information Disclosure Statements (37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98), see MPEP §609 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section points examiners and practitioners to MPEP §609 for procedures regarding how IDS citations are considered/recorded; do not assume the Search Notes will reflect IDS consideration — follow MPEP §609 procedures for details.
